definitions.meaning: A count out of one hundred: 25% is 25 out of 100, whatever the whole in the question is.
A square split into one hundred equal cells for picturing a percent: twenty-five shaded cells out of one hundred is 25%.
One of four equal parts of a whole: 25 out of 100 simplifies to one quarter, so 25% of a quantity is a quarter of it.
The full amount the percent is taken of: in 25% of 60 the whole is 60, so the answer is a share of 60.

mechanismSteps: Percent means per hundred: shade twenty-five cells out of one hundred on the hundred-grid - that shaded amount is 25%.
Watch out: 25% is not just 25: the 25 counts out of one hundred, and the whole here is 60, so the answer is a share of 60, not 25 itself.
25% of 60: divide into quarters: 25 out of 100 simplifies to one quarter, so split 60 into four equal parts and take one: 60 / 4 = 15.
The takeaway: a percent is out of one hundred - turn it into a fraction of the whole first, and 25% of 60 comes out as one quarter of 60, which is 15.
objectives: Read a percent as a count out of one hundred: 25% as 25 out of 100
Find a percent of a quantity by turning it into a fraction of the whole: 25% as one quarter
subject: math
title: Percentage: 25% of 60

trap.explanation: The 25 is read as a raw count instead of 25 out of 100. Percent means per hundred, and the whole here is 60: 25% of 60 is a quarter of 60, which is 15. In the animation scene s2 the claim is tested against the hundred-grid and fails: the 25 belongs to the hundred, never to the 60.

workedExample: In scene s3, 25% of 60 is worked by seeing the percent as a fraction first: 25% is 25 out of 100, which simplifies to one quarter. Step by step: 25% = 1/4, then 60 / 4 = 15.
